title: What are the Solvency II fit and proper requirements for insurers?
seoTitle: Solvency II fit and proper rules
description: Solvency II fit and proper rules: Article 42, Delegated Regulation Article 273, EIOPA governance guidelines, and the Directive (EU) 2025/2 changes from 2027.
shortAnswer: Article 42 of the Solvency II Directive (2009/138/EC) requires every EU insurer and reinsurer to ensure that the people who effectively run it or hold other key functions are at all times fit, meaning adequately qualified, knowledgeable and experienced, and proper, meaning of good repute and integrity. Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Article 273 requires documented fit and proper policies, and Directive (EU) 2025/2 adds supervisory removal powers from 30 January 2027.
keyTakeaways: Article 42(1) applies at all times to everyone who effectively runs the undertaking or has other key functions; fitness covers professional qualifications, knowledge and experience, and propriety covers good repute and integrity.

Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Article 273 requires documented policies and adequate procedures, assesses fitness against the duties allocated to each person, and assesses propriety on honesty and financial soundness.

EIOPA's Guidelines on system of governance (EIOPA-BoS-14/253) Guidelines 11 to 16 add that the board must collectively know five named areas and that the fit and proper policy must cover reassessment triggers and outsourced key functions.

Directive (EU) 2025/2 must be transposed by January 29, 2027 and applied from January 30, 2027. It requires reasons for changes in key personnel, notification when a person stops meeting the requirements, and a supervisory power to require removal.

The review also adds a board diversity policy with gender-balance objectives, separate persons for the four key functions (with exceptions for small and non-complex undertakings), and a remuneration written policy.
jurisdiction: European Union (all EU Member States; Solvency II Directive 2009/138/EC as transposed into national law, and directly applicable Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35)
regulator: National insurance supervisory authorities in each Member State, coordinated by the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA); legislation adopted by the European Parliament, the Council and the European Commission
appliesTo: Insurance and reinsurance undertakings authorized under Solvency II
Members of the administrative, management or supervisory body and others who effectively run the undertaking
Holders of the risk management, compliance, internal audit and actuarial key functions
Persons performing outsourced key functions, and insurance holding companies through Article 257

sections.heading: What does Article 42 of Solvency II require?

blocks.text: Article 42 requires insurers and reinsurers to ensure that everyone who effectively runs the undertaking or has other key functions meets two tests continuously, not only at appointment. The text below is from the consolidated [Solvency II Directive 2009/138/EC](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02009L0138-20250117) on EUR-Lex, as at November 2026.

blocks.title: Solvency II Directive, Article 42(1)
blocks.text: "Insurance and reinsurance undertakings shall ensure that all persons who effectively run the undertaking or have other key functions at all times fulfil the following requirements: (a) their professional qualifications, knowledge and experience are adequate to enable sound and prudent management (fit); and (b) they are of good repute and integrity (proper)."

Article 42(2) requires the undertaking to notify its supervisory authority of any change in the identity of these persons, with the information needed to assess whether new appointees are fit and proper. Article 42(3) requires notification when a person has been replaced because they no longer meet the requirements. Article 43 governs cross-border proof of good repute: an extract from the judicial record or an equivalent document from the home Member State must be accepted, and such documents may not be presented more than three months after issue.

Article 42 sits inside the system of governance in Article 41, which must be proportionate to the nature, scale and complexity of the operations, be subject to regular internal review, and include written policies on at least risk management, internal control, internal audit and, where relevant, outsourcing, reviewed at least annually.

sections.heading: How does Delegated Regulation 2015/35 Article 273 define fit and proper?

blocks.text: [Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015R0035) Article 273 turns the Directive's two tests into an assessment method and requires the undertaking to document it. The regulation applies directly in every Member State without transposition.

items: **Policies and procedures (Article 273(1)):** documented policies and adequate procedures to ensure all persons who effectively run the undertaking or have other key functions are at all times fit and proper.

**Fitness of individuals (273(2)):** an assessment of professional and formal qualifications, knowledge and relevant experience within insurance, other financial sectors or other businesses, taking account of the duties allocated and, where relevant, insurance, financial, accounting, actuarial and management skills.

**Fitness of the board (273(3)):** the assessment of members of the administrative, management or supervisory body takes account of the duties allocated to each member, to ensure appropriate diversity of qualifications, knowledge and relevant experience.

**Propriety (273(4)):** an assessment of honesty and financial soundness based on evidence about character, personal behavior and business conduct, including any criminal, financial and supervisory aspects.

blocks.text: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/269 of October 29, 2025, published in the Official Journal on February 18, 2026 and applying from January 30, 2027, amends Delegated Regulation 2015/35 to implement the Solvency II review. The EUR-Lex amendment history shows no substantive change to Article 273. The amended reporting rules restate that the regular supervisory report must list the persons responsible for key functions and describe the undertaking's specific requirements for skills, knowledge and expertise (Article 308(2)).

sections.heading: What do the EIOPA governance guidelines add?

blocks.text: EIOPA's [Guidelines on system of governance](https://www.eiopa.europa.eu/publications/guidelines-system-governance_en) (EIOPA-BoS-14/253), which apply from January 1, 2016, add detail on board knowledge, the content of the fit and proper policy and outsourcing. They are issued under Article 16 of the EIOPA Regulation, under which supervisors and undertakings must make every effort to comply, and supervisors must confirm to EIOPA whether they comply, with reasons for any non-compliance.

items: **Guideline 11, collective knowledge:** the administrative, management or supervisory body should collectively possess appropriate qualification, experience and knowledge about at least insurance and financial markets, business strategy and business model, system of governance, financial and actuarial analysis, and regulatory framework and requirements.
**Guideline 12, propriety:** when assessing propriety, the undertaking should consider whether the period of limitation of a relevant offense has lapsed under national law.

**Guideline 13, the policy:** the fit and proper policy should describe how positions requiring notification are identified, how fitness and propriety are assessed at appointment and on an ongoing basis, which situations trigger reassessment, and how other relevant personnel outside Article 42 are assessed against internal standards.

**Guideline 14, outsourcing:** fit and proper procedures apply to service provider staff performing an outsourced key function, and the undertaking must designate an internal person with overall responsibility who is fit and proper and able to challenge the provider.
**Guidelines 15 and 16:** supervisors should require notification content set out in a technical annex and assess notified persons, giving feedback within an appropriate timeframe.

sections.heading: What changes under the Solvency II review, and when?

blocks.text: [Directive (EU) 2025/2](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32025L0002), published in the Official Journal on January 8, 2025, amends Solvency II. Under its Article 4, Member States must adopt and publish transposing measures by January 29, 2027 and apply them from January 30, 2027. Until then, the current Article 42 text applies.

Point (21) of Article 1 replaces Article 42(2) and (3) and adds a paragraph 4. Notifications of changes in key personnel must now include the reasons for the change. Undertakings must notify the supervisor if a person no longer meets the requirements, not only when the person has been replaced for that reason. New Article 42(4) gives supervisors the power to require the undertaking to remove a person who does not meet the requirements. Recital 67 explains that people should be fit and proper on a continuous basis.

The same Directive amends Article 41. The internal review of the system of governance must include an assessment of the composition, effectiveness and internal governance of the board; undertakings must adopt a board diversity policy with individual quantitative gender-balance objectives; and new Article 41(2a) requires different persons for the risk management, actuarial, compliance and internal audit functions. Small and non-complex undertakings, or those with prior supervisory approval, may combine functions other than internal audit if conflicts are managed. Written policies now include remuneration, and small and non-complex undertakings may review them at least every five years.

sections.heading: How should an insurer evidence fit and proper compliance?

blocks.text: Supervisors look for a documented policy, an assessment file per person, and proof that assessments are repeated when circumstances change. The table maps each obligation to the role and the evidence a supervisor would expect.

blocks.text: Fitness is not a one-time credential. Because Article 42 says "at all times," knowledge must keep pace with new rules, which is where structured training for board members and key function holders becomes evidence. The guide on [mapping training to compliance obligations](/guides/how-to-map-training-to-compliance-obligations) shows how to tie each training item to the obligation it supports, and the [guide to reporting training compliance to the board](/guides/how-to-report-training-compliance-to-the-board) covers how to present it.

sections.heading: How does this relate to other EU and national regimes?

blocks.text: Solvency II fit and proper rules cover senior management and key functions, not sales staff. Knowledge and competence for employees who distribute insurance is governed by the Insurance Distribution Directive, described on the page on [IDD continuing professional development requirements](/regulations/insurance-distribution-directive-cpd-requirements). Pension funds follow the parallel but differently worded regime in the page on [IORP II fit and proper requirements](/regulations/iorp-ii-pension-fund-fit-and-proper).

Banks apply the comparable EBA framework covered on the page on [EBA internal governance and staff training](/regulations/eba-internal-governance-staff-training). Insurers also need ICT knowledge at board level under DORA, which Article 41(4) of Solvency II now cross-references; see [DORA ICT security awareness training](/regulations/dora-ict-security-awareness-training).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps the GL 11 knowledge areas, each key function's responsibilities and the 2027 review changes into a framework of required knowledge per role. Board and key function training then links to specific gaps in the skills matrix, so the assessment file shows why each person remains fit, not just which courses they attended.

faqs.q: Who counts as a key function holder under Solvency II?
faqs.a: The four functions named in the review's new Article 41(2a) are risk management, actuarial, compliance and internal audit. EIOPA Guideline 14 adds that when a key function is outsourced, an internal person with overall responsibility must be designated, and that person is notified to the supervisor.

faqs.q: Does the supervisor approve appointments in advance?
faqs.a: Article 42 of the Directive is built on notification: the undertaking notifies changes and the supervisor assesses the person, as EIOPA Guideline 16 describes. National law may add more, so check the local regime. From January 30, 2027, Directive (EU) 2025/2 gives every supervisor the power to require removal of a person who does not meet the fit and proper requirements.

faqs.q: Does every board member need actuarial expertise?
faqs.a: No. Article 273(3) assesses board fitness taking account of each member's duties, and EIOPA Guideline 11 expects the body to collectively possess knowledge of the five listed areas. Individual members bring different strengths, provided the collective coverage is adequate and documented.

faqs.q: Do fit and proper rules apply to insurance holding companies?
faqs.a: Yes. Article 257, as replaced by Directive (EU) 2025/2, requires those who effectively run an insurance holding company or mixed financial holding company, and where applicable persons responsible for other key functions, to be fit and proper, and applies Article 42 mutatis mutandis.

factCheck.claim: Solvency II Article 42(1) fit (professional qualifications, knowledge and experience) and proper (good repute and integrity) at all times; 42(2) notification of changes; 42(3) notification of replacement; Article 43(3) documents not more than three months after issue; Article 41 proportionality, internal review, written policies reviewed at least annually.

Delegated Regulation 2015/35 Article 273(1) to (4): documented policies; fitness assessment of qualifications, knowledge, experience and skills; board diversity of qualifications; propriety assessment of honesty and financial soundness.

Directive (EU) 2025/2, OJ 8.1.2025: Article 4 transposition by 29 January 2027, apply from 30 January 2027; Article 1 point (21) replaces Article 42(2) and (3) and adds 42(4) removal power; Article 41 amendments on board review, diversity policy with gender-balance objectives, new 41(2a) separate key function holders with SNCU exceptions, remuneration policy and five-year review for SNCUs; Article 257 replaced; recital 67.

Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/269 of 29 October 2025, OJ L 18.2.2026, applies from 30 January 2027; Article 308(2) RSR content on fit and proper; EUR-Lex amendment list for 32015R0035 shows Article 273 modified only by a German-language correction (32016R2283).

EIOPA-BoS-14/253 Guidelines on system of governance: apply from 1 January 2016; Guideline 11 collective knowledge of five areas; Guideline 12 limitation periods; Guideline 13 fit and proper policy content; Guideline 14 outsourced key functions and designated person; Guidelines 15 and 16 notification and supervisory assessment.
